blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
In industries where talent is scarce and highly mobile, the quality of talent acquisition is no longer a back-office concern — it is a genuine source of competitive advantage. Companies that consistently hire better than their competitors compound that advantage over years, sometimes decades.

What separates the best from the rest is not the sophistication of their tools, but the discipline of their choices. They invest in deep understanding of the roles that matter most, and they build long-term relationships with candidates they are not yet ready to hire. They refuse to compromise on the few characteristics that predict success, while remaining genuinely open on those that do not.

The weakest acquisition functions behave reactively — filling vacancies as they appear, with little strategic view. The strongest build a proactive pipeline, often bringing in talent before there is an open role. The return on that investment is not always visible in quarterly KPIs, but it shows up unmistakably in the quality of leadership five years later.

items.q: According to the text, why has talent acquisition stopped being a back-office concern?
options: Because it is a genuine source of competitive advantage
Because vacancies appear more frequently than before
Because quarterly KPIs now measure it precisely
Because hiring tools have become far cheaper
items.why: "it is no longer a back-office concern — it is a genuine source of competitive advantage."

items.q: What does the text say separates the best acquisition functions from the rest?
options: The size of their recruiting team
The speed at which they fill vacancies
items.why: "not the sophistication of their tools, but the discipline of their choices."

items.q: The author suggests that building relationships with candidates "not yet ready to hire" reflects…
options: an unnecessary cost with no return
a way to lower quarterly hiring costs
a reactive stance driven by open vacancies
a proactive, long-term view of talent
items.why: Inferência: cultivar candidatos antes de haver vaga é a postura proativa e de longo prazo defendida no texto.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: A proactive pipeline can precede an open role
The best hires demand discipline over tooling
Talent acquisition can compound advantage over years
Judging talent acquisition by quarterly KPIs captures its full value
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que o retorno "nem sempre é visível nos KPIs trimestrais", mas aparece na liderança cinco anos depois.

items.q: The final sentence about "the quality of leadership five years later" suggests that…
options: the payoff of good sourcing is delayed but real
quarterly metrics are the only reliable measure
leadership quality cannot be influenced by hiring
items.why: Inferência: o benefício não aparece já, mas se materializa anos depois — retorno diferido, porém concreto.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Oliver defendendo o orçamento de aquisição de talentos diante do CFO. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
I know the number looks uncomfortable, so let me be clear about what we are actually buying. We are not buying more recruiters. We are buying a proactive pipeline — relationships with people we may not hire for eighteen months, in the two or three roles that genuinely move this business.

Right now we hire reactively. A seat opens, we panic, we take whoever is available in six weeks. That candidate is rarely the best predictor of success — just the fastest to close. And in a market this tight, the best people are never on the market. Our competitors are already trying to poach them.

So here is the trade-off I am asking you to accept. This spend will not show up in a single quarter. There is no line in Q3 that says "leadership crisis avoided". What I can promise is that in two to three years, the quality of the people running our regions will be visibly better than our rivals' — because we will have been talking to them for years, not weeks.

If you want me to defend this on quarterly KPIs alone, I will lose. Judge it on the calibre of leadership we build, and it is the cheapest investment on this table.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: According to Oliver, what is the budget actually buying?
options: A proactive pipeline of long-term candidate relationships
items.why: "We are not buying more recruiters. We are buying a proactive pipeline."

items.q: What does Oliver say is wrong with the current reactive approach?
options: It relies too heavily on external agencies
It ignores the opinions of hiring managers
It hires the fastest candidate rather than the best predictor of success
It costs more per hire than proactive sourcing
items.why: "That candidate is rarely the best predictor of success — just the fastest to close."

items.q: Why does Oliver say the best people are "never on the market"?
options: They only respond to higher salaries
They are being actively poached by competitors
They are unaware of new opportunities
items.why: "the best people are never on the market. Our competitors are already trying to poach them."

items.q: What does Oliver mean by "There is no line in Q3 that says 'leadership crisis avoided'"?
options: The CFO should add a new KPI to the report
The company has never faced a leadership crisis
Q3 is the wrong quarter to launch the initiative
The value of the spend cannot be captured in a single quarter's metrics
items.why: Inferência: ele admite que o retorno é intangível no curto prazo — não cabe numa métrica trimestral.

items.q: How would you best describe Oliver's argumentative strategy with the CFO?
options: He threatens to resign if the budget is cut
He concedes the short-term weakness but reframes the metric for judging success
He appeals purely to emotion and urgency
He denies there is any trade-off at all
items.why: Inferência: ele reconhece que perderia nos KPIs trimestrais, mas pede que julguem pelo calibre da liderança — reenquadra o critério.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Hiring better than rivals is a durable competitive advantage." A competitive advantage is…
options: a temporary discount on recruiting costs
an edge that lets a company outperform its rivals
items.why: Competitive advantage = vantagem competitiva: aquilo que faz a empresa superar os concorrentes.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "In a market of severe talent ___, the best candidates are never actively looking."
items.why: Talent scarcity = escassez de talentos; num mercado escasso os melhores nem estão à procura.

items.q: "A small edge, repeated every year, will compound." To compound here means to…
items.why: To compound = acumular com o tempo, crescer de forma composta.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "The strongest teams build a ___ — bringing in talent before a role even opens."
items.why: Proactive pipeline = pipeline proativo: talento cultivado antes de existir a vaga.

items.q: "We only ever fill seats after they open — pure reactive hiring." Reactive hiring is…
options: recruiting only in response to vacancies, with little strategic view
items.why: Reactive hiring = contratação reativa: preencher vagas conforme surgem, sem visão estratégica.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em reuniões sobre aquisição de talentos. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The CFO still has to sign off on the increased budget." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We plan to roll out the new sourcing model across all regions next year." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "Finance pushed back on the extra headcount." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "We agreed the pipeline plan but never followed through." They…
options: handed it to a rival firm
failed to see it through to the end
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado — aqui, o que não aconteceu.

items.q: "Cheaper job ads will not move the needle on the quality of our hires." This means they will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível; aqui, negado.
